newsitem.title: UK: UK homes, offices rush to link up to cable - CCA.
newsitem.headline: UK homes, offices rush to link up to cable - CCA.

text.p: A record number of UK homes and businesses are linking up to cable television and telephone services, the Cable Communications Association (CCA) said on Monday.

More than 10 percent of British homes are now connected to the cable broadband fibre optic network, and in the last quarter more homes than ever before -- over 600,000 -- were passed by the cable network, allowing them to get connected, the CCA said.

Thirty percent of all homes passed now take advantage of cable's extra programme choice and high quality, low-cost telephone services in an industry whose annual revenues exceed 1.0 billion stg, the CCA said.

"The lastest figures show that given the choice, significant numbers of both business and domestic consumers are increasingly taking advantage of the competitiveness of cable's broadband fibre optic technology and the services it can deliver," said CCA chief executive Bob Frost in a statement.

According to figures from the Independent Television Commission (ITC) quarterly cable statistics, the last year has seen the number of residential cable telephone customers jump nearly 65 percent to 1.8 million.

Over the same period, there has been a 78 percent rise in business cable telephony connections to 2.02 million from 1.22 million -- and 7.8 million homes are now passed by the broadband fibre optic network, 40 percent more than last year.
The number of cable television customers has also risen 42 percnt to 1.65 million and over 2.0 million cable telephone lines are now connected, according to the CCA.
